changes.pattern: Actor loops on the same failed or post-completion command (examine, inventory, done, go-to, help, look) dozens of times, burning all 40 steps without completing the task.
changes.rationale: The actor role has no anti-looping rule, no correct placement command (it uses 'put' which always returns 'Nothing happens'; the environment requires 'move {obj} to {recep}'), no task-completion signal (so it keeps acting after the goal is met), and no appliance-mechanics guidance (so it puts the object inside the microwave/fridge instead of just running the command). All four failures are visible across the wrong traces: A41 loops 'examine shelf 1' ×40; A2 loops 'inventory' ×30 after 'put towel 1 in drawer 1' fails; A56 loops 'go to cabinet 2' ×35; A45 loops 'done' ×25 after the mug is already on the countertop; A21 puts the potato inside the microwave then cannot heat it; A44 puts the mug inside the microwave. Adding these four always-on rules to the actor role directly addresses each root cause.

ops.name: actor
ops.role:
You act in a household text environment. Each turn: 'Think: ...' then 'Action: <one command>'.
- To place an object: move {obj} to {recep}.
- If a command returns 'Nothing happens', do not repeat it. Try a different command or go to a new location.
- When the task goal is met, only use 'look' or 'inventory' for remaining steps.
- For heat, cool, or clean: go to the appliance while holding the object, then run the command. Do not open the appliance or put the object inside it.

changes.pattern: Planner omits key intermediate steps (take the object, go to the lamp, use the lamp; clean; heat; cool) from the written plan, so the actor skips or misinterprets the required action sequence.
changes.rationale: In all three look_in_light wrong tasks the planner's plan is incomplete or wrong: A41 says 'confirm the pencil is under the desklamp' without saying take-then-use; A124 says 'inspect the bed area underneath it' instead of take-pillow-go-to-lamp-use-lamp; A148 says 'use lamp (if a lamp is present) or examine laptop' which is vague. The planner role currently only says 'where to look first and the steps to finish' without requiring every intermediate action to be listed. Adding 'including every intermediate action (take, clean, heat, cool, use lamp)' forces the planner to write a complete step-by-step sequence, which the actor can then follow.

ops.name: planner
ops.role: You read the task and the room, and write a short plan for the teammate who will act: where to look first and the exact steps to finish, listing every intermediate action (take, clean, heat, cool, use lamp) in order. You do not act.

changes.pattern: Actor uses invalid 'put {obj} in/on {recep}' command (not a real command) and then loops repeating the same failing command, exhausting all 40 steps
changes.rationale: The environment's help output shows only 'move (object) to (receptacle)' as the placement command; 'put' is not valid. The action_syntax skill teaches 'put {obj} in/on {recep}', so the actor types it, gets 'Nothing happens', and then repeats the same command 20-40 times (A2 inventory loop, A3 go-to-cabinet loop, A46 move loop, A18 put loop, A56 go-to-cabinet loop). Fixing the command to 'move {obj} to {recep}' and adding an explicit anti-repeat instruction in the same skill addresses both the wrong syntax and the loop.

ops.name: action_syntax
ops.text: Commands: go to {recep}; open {recep}; close {recep}; take {obj} from {recep}; move {obj} to {recep}; clean {obj} with {sinkbasin}; heat {obj} with {microwave}; cool {obj} with {fridge}; use {lamp}; examine {obj or recep}; inventory; look. Use the exact names with numbers as they appear ('mug 1', 'countertop 2'). You can hold one object; you must be at a receptacle to take from or move to it. If 'Nothing happens' appears the command was invalid: do NOT type the same command again; read the valid_actions list and pick a different one.

ops.name: pick_place
ops.when: put an object in/on a receptacle
ops.text: 1. Find the object (search_order), take it. The object name must match the task exactly (a mug is not a cup, a towel is not a cloth, a handtowel is not a cloth). 2. Go to the target receptacle; open it if closed. 3. move {obj} to {recep}. The task is done when the object is placed.

ops.name: pick_two
ops.when: put two objects of a type in/on a receptacle
ops.text: 1. Find the first object, take it, move it to the target. 2. Go back to searching for the second one (it may be elsewhere; remember where you saw others). 3. Move the second to the same target. You can carry only one object at a time. The object name must match the task exactly.

ops.name: heat_task
ops.when: put a hot or heated object somewhere
ops.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to microwave 1, then 'heat {obj} with microwave 1'. You must be standing at the microwave and holding the object. Do NOT open the microwave. Do NOT put the object inside the microwave. 3. Go to the target, open it if needed, move {obj} to {target}.

ops.name: cool_task
ops.when: put a cool or cold object somewhere
ops.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to fridge 1, then 'cool {obj} with fridge 1'. You must be standing at the fridge and holding the object. Do NOT open the fridge. Do NOT put the object inside the fridge. 3. Go to the target, open it if needed, move {obj} to {target}. If the target is the fridge itself this is a plain placement.

ops.name: clean_task
ops.text: 1. Find and take the object. The object name must match the task exactly (a towel is not a cloth, a handtowel is not a cloth). 2. go to sinkbasin 1 (or the sinkbasin), then 'clean {obj} with sinkbasin 1'. 3. Go to the target, open it if needed, move {obj} to {target}. Do not put the object in the sink to clean it; use the clean command.

ops.name: search_order
ops.when: the target object is not in view (most tasks)
ops.text: Search likely places first and never revisit a place you have checked. Typical: food (apple, potato, tomato, egg, lettuce, bread) -> fridge, countertop, diningtable, sinkbasin, garbagecan; dishes (mug, cup, plate, bowl, pan, pot) -> countertop, cabinet, diningtable, sinkbasin, shelf, drawer; small items (keychain, creditcard, pen, pencil, cd, cellphone) -> desk, drawer, sidetable, dresser, shelf; towels/cloth/soap -> towelholder, countertop, toilet, cabinet, bathtubbasin; books/laptops -> desk, bed, sofa, sidetable. Open closed cabinets, drawers, fridges and safes to see inside. Search for the exact object name in the task (cloth is not towel, cup is not mug).

Give the skill matching the task type: look_in_light for 'look at X under lamp', heat_task for heating, cool_task for cooling, clean_task for cleaning, pick_two for two objects, pick_place for single placement. Always also give action_syntax to the actor.

changes.pattern: Agents use the non-existent 'put' command to place objects; the environment only supports 'move {obj} to {recep}', causing placement failures and subsequent stuck loops
changes.rationale: In A2, A18, A46, A63 the agent types 'put X in/on Y' which returns 'Nothing happens', while 'move X to Y' succeeds (seen in A45, A18, A46 after the agent discovers it). The action_syntax skill explicitly teaches the wrong verb. Fixing the skill to say 'move' aligns the instruction with the environment's actual command set (confirmed by the 'help' output in A17/A42 traces).

ops.name: action_syntax
ops.text: Commands: go to {recep}; open {recep}; close {recep}; take {obj} from {recep}; move {obj} to {recep}; clean {obj} with {sinkbasin}; heat {obj} with {microwave}; cool {obj} with {fridge}; use {lamp}; examine {obj or recep}; inventory; look. Use the exact names with numbers as they appear ('mug 1', 'countertop 2'). You can hold one object; you must be at a receptacle to take from or move to it. 'Nothing happens' means the command was invalid: change it.

changes.pattern: Agents get stuck repeating the same failing command 20-30 times (inventory, examine, go-to, look) and never recover; they also substitute a similar-but-wrong object type (mug for cup, towel for cloth)
changes.rationale: Traces A41 (examine shelf 1 ×30), A2 (inventory ×30), A3 (go to cabinet 13 ×14), A56 (go to cabinet 2 ×30), A124 (look shelf 2 ×30), A45 (done ×30) all show the same loop. The stuck_recovery skill is given to only 1 node. Since looping and wrong-object-substitution occur on every task type, the fix belongs in the actor's always-on role, not a per-task skill.

ops.name: actor
ops.role: You act in a household text environment to complete the task. Each turn, write one short line 'Think: ...' and then 'Action: <one command>'. Use the exact object type named in the task (a mug is not a cup, a towel is not a cloth). If a command returns 'Nothing happens', do not repeat it; try a different command or go to a different location.

changes.pattern: On heat tasks the agent puts the object inside the microwave (open, move-in, close) and then the heat command fails because the object is no longer in hand; the correct procedure is to heat while holding the object at the microwave
changes.rationale: A21: agent opens microwave, moves potato inside, closes it, then 'heat potato 3 with microwave 1' → Nothing happens. A44: same pattern with mug. In A45 the agent correctly goes to microwave while holding the mug and heats it (succeeds). The skill already says 'no need to open or put inside' but agents ignore it; making it a negative imperative ('Do NOT') and adding 'while holding the object' makes the constraint harder to miss.

ops.name: heat_task
ops.when: put a hot or heated object somewhere
ops.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to microwave 1 while holding the object, then 'heat {obj} with microwave 1'. Do NOT open the microwave. Do NOT put the object inside it. 3. Go to the target receptacle, open it if closed, then 'move {obj} to {target}'.

changes.pattern: On cool tasks the agent puts the object inside the fridge (open, move-in, take-out) without ever running the cool command while holding it, so the object is never actually cooled
changes.rationale: A38: agent moves pan into fridge, takes it out, never runs 'cool pan 1 with fridge 1' while at the fridge → pan is not cool → task fails. A42: agent first tries cool from afar (fails), then at fridge opens it and cools (succeeds) but used wrong object type. A17: similar fridge-interaction confusion. Same fix as heat: emphasize holding the object and not putting it inside.

ops.name: cool_task
ops.when: put a cool or cold object somewhere
ops.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to fridge 1 while holding the object, then 'cool {obj} with fridge 1'. Do NOT open the fridge. Do NOT put the object inside it. 3. Go to the target receptacle, open it if closed, then 'move {obj} to {target}'. If the target is the fridge itself, just 'move {obj} to fridge 1'.

changes.pattern: On clean tasks the agent puts the object into the sink or uses 'move' to the sink instead of running the clean command while holding it at the sink, and then uses the wrong placement command
changes.rationale: A19: agent moves handtowel to sinkbasin, takes it back, then can't place it. A48: agent tries 'clean towel 1 with sinkbasin 1' → Nothing happens (was holding towel but at wrong sink or syntax issue), then loops on examine. A63: 'clean towel 1 with sinkbasin 1' → Nothing happens, then 'put towel 1 in toilet 1' → Nothing happens. Fix: clarify holding-at-sink and use 'move' for final placement.

ops.name: clean_task
ops.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to sinkbasin 1 while holding the object, then 'clean {obj} with sinkbasin 1'. Do NOT put the object in the sink. 3. Go to the target receptacle, open it if closed, then 'move {obj} to {target}'.

changes.pattern: Meta-agent fails to give look_in_light skill for 'look at X under lamp' tasks, so the actor searches for the object but never learns to hold it while using the lamp
changes.rationale: A41: actor gets search_order+action_syntax but NOT look_in_light → finds pencil, loops on examine. A124: actor gets only search_order → finds lamp, turns it on without holding pillow, gets confused. A148: actor gets only action_syntax → finds laptop, puts it down, uses lamp without holding it. Rule 3 says 'Give the skill for the task type' but the 9B meta-agent doesn't map 'look under lamp' to look_in_light. Making the mapping explicit in the rule fixes the staffing.

ops.text: Give the actor the skill for the task type: 'look at X under lamp'→look_in_light; 'clean X and put'→clean_task; 'hot X'/'heat X'→heat_task; 'cool X'/'cold X'→cool_task; 'two X'→pick_two; 'put a X'→pick_place. Always also give search_order and action_syntax to the actor.

changes.pattern: On look-in-light tasks the agent finds the lamp and turns it on without holding the target object, or puts the object down before using the lamp, so the task is never completed
changes.rationale: A124: agent uses desklamp 1 (turns it on) while NOT holding the pillow, then goes to bed and gets lost in spatial reasoning. A148: agent takes laptop, moves it to desk (puts it down), then uses desklamp without holding the laptop. A41: agent never finds the lamp, loops on examine. The skill needs to stress 'keep holding the object the entire time' and give a concrete search order for both the target object and the lamp.

ops.name: look_in_light
ops.when: examine or look at an object with/under a lamp
ops.text: 1. Find the target object (check desk, shelf, bed, sidetable) and take it. 2. Find a desklamp or floorlamp (check desk, sidetable, dresser, shelf). 3. Go to the lamp while holding the object, then 'use {lamp}'. This completes the task. Keep holding the object the entire time; do not put it down before using the lamp.

changes.pattern: On simple pick-and-place tasks the agent picks a similar-but-wrong object (mug for cup, towel for cloth) and/or uses the wrong placement command, so the grader finds the wrong object at the target
changes.rationale: A45: task says 'cup', agent picks mug → grader fails. A44: task says 'cup', agent first picks mug, later finds cup but wastes steps. A19: task says 'cloth', agent picks handtowel then towel. A2: task says 'cloth', agent picks towel. The pick_place skill mentions the pitfall in one sentence but it is buried; making the object-type check step 1 and using 'move' for placement addresses both issues in the skill the meta-agent gives for every single-place task.

ops.name: pick_place
ops.when: put an object in/on a receptacle
ops.text: 1. Find the exact object type named in the task (a cup is not a mug, a cloth is not a towel, a pan is not a pot), take it. 2. Go to the target receptacle; open it if closed. 3. move {obj} to {recep}. The task is done when the object is placed.
